focus: History after compaction (v4.0.2.0): the read-only session lookup, its per-runtime producers, its refusal paths and its read-only guarantee
answeredQuestions: History after compaction (v4.0.2.0): does the session history lookup (.opencode/plugins/session-history-lookup.js and its counterparts) stay read-only and work on each runtime the note names?

graphEvents.label: Does the history lookup stay read-only and work on every runtime the note names?
Offer command points at a gitignored dist artifact, so an unbuilt copy has no feature
Help line's operations cannot run as printed; CLI refuses on missing cd and runtime prefix
Two producers duplicate the same dynamic support probe
Runtime label set enumerated twice, capability table and CLI can disagree
Codex marked ready but its offer depends on a transcript path its adapter does not require
Section size bound asserted by a test, not enforced by the builder
History lookup is read-only across library, CLI and all seven stores

label: The history-lookup offer command hardcodes the gitignored dist/ CLI path, and buildHistoryLookupSection returns null when that file is absent, so a fresh clone or vendored copy with no local build shows no ## History Lookup section at all and gives no diagnostic. The note presents the feature as shipped and defers the build to a one-line upgrade note.

The printed primary command carries both the cd to the checkout root and the SPECKIT_RUNTIME prefix, but the follow-up line lists search/load/page as bare JSON with neither, while the CLI refuses independently on runtime_mismatch and workspace_mismatch. A model that keeps the working command and swaps the operation gets a refusal envelope instead of history, and the risk is highest on the five non-Claude runtimes where the prefix is mandatory.

The OpenCode plugin and the DSH hook each hand-write a dynamic import of the same six compiled history symbols and re-check their types, and each repeats the reader module path. Collapsing the guard into one compiled loadHistorySupport() removes both copies; nothing breaks at runtime because each runtime's hook registration must stay regardless.

The runtime label set is enumerated twice: capabilities in the session-reader dispatcher and a hard-coded pi/devin/dsh/opencode list in the CLI's currentRuntime(). The CLI refuses unsupported_runtime before consulting the capability table, so a reader added to the table but missed in the list is unreachable.

Hypothesis, not confirmed: Codex reaches the Claude PreCompact adapter with SPECKIT_RUNTIME=codex and the reader capability row says ready, but minting also needs a non-empty transcript_path and a basename ending -<sessionId>.jsonl, while the Codex adapter requires only session_id. If the live Codex payload omits or renames transcript_path the section never appears and nothing says why.

HISTORY_LOOKUP_MAX_CHARS is 600 and the offer builder never measures itself against it; the only enforcement is a test assertion, so a longer runtime prefix or session id would ship an over-budget section and fail CI instead of failing closed at runtime.

History lookup is read-only across the library and CLI: zero matches for write, network or process APIs; the CLI reads hook state directly instead of the migrating loader so a refusal cannot cause a quarantine or migration write; both SQLite readers open { readOnly: true }; the side-effect suite reports all seven stores unchanged in bytes, sizes and mtimes.

The 30-minute handle in the release note matches code on both sides: LOCATOR_TTL_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000 in the CLI and the same bound in the producer that stops re-offering, with a future timestamp treated as stale rather than fresh.

node --test .opencode/plugins/tests/session-history-lookup.test.cjs exits 0 with 3/3 pass: offer mints, redeems from a subfolder, a second request keeps the offer, a folder outside any checkout gets none.
node --test .skilled/hooks/shared/tests/session-readers/ exits 0 with 85/85 pass and logs 'stores unchanged: 7', confirming every reader leaves store bytes, sizes and mtimes identical.

direction: Cursor history lookup is a wiring gap the release note failed to disclose
reason: The note says Cursor is not supported yet and the code agrees: cursor.mjs returns capability_gated before touching any file and locator_unavailable even with the operator switch on, and detectHistoryRuntime returns null for the cursor label so no locator is ever minted.

direction: Codex hook adapters are broken because .codex/hooks/compact-inject.js imports a nonexistent ./shared.js
reason: False positive: .codex/hooks entries are symlinks into runtime/dist/hooks/codex/, where shared.js and ../claude/directive-lifecycle-boundary.js both exist, and hooks.json invokes the real dist path rather than the mirror.
